title: Recognizing minimally false quantified formulas of fixed deficiency
formal: Editorial tractability variant: for every fixed integer k≥2, is the language MF(k) of minimally false closed prenex CNF quantified Boolean formulas of raw deficiency k decidable in deterministic polynomial time?
definitions:
A formula is Q_1 x_1 … Q_v x_v . C, with each Q_i either forall or exists, each variable quantified exactly once, and C an explicitly written conjunction of clauses. Clauses are finite sets of literals, with no repeated literal or complementary pair, and the matrix has no repeated clauses. Every prefix variable appears in the matrix. The empty clause is allowed. Formula size counts its explicit prefix and literal lists with binary variable indices. Truth is the usual quantified Boolean semantics: an existential value may depend on earlier universal choices, not later ones.

The formula is minimally false when it is false and deleting any one clause, while retaining the prefix, makes it true. Write m for the number of clauses and e for the number of existential variables occurring in the original matrix; raw deficiency is m−e. MF(k) consists of syntactically valid formulas of deficiency exactly k that are minimally false. Inputs of other deficiencies or invalid syntax are rejected, so this is a total language, not a promise to be false or minimal. The integer k is fixed outside the input; the algorithm and polynomial exponent may depend on k. Raw deficiency is not the maximum deficiency among subformulas.

This selects the polynomial-time tractability question from the source’s broader request to determine exact complexity. It does not assert that a negative answer automatically entails DP-completeness.
answer_criterion: Prove in Lean that MF(k) has a polynomial-time decider for every fixed k≥2, or prove that this fails for at least one specified fixed k. A conditional hardness result must state its assumption and yields only a conditional negative answer. A bound polynomial when maximal deficiency is fixed does not suffice without connecting that parameter to this language.
context: Kleine Büning’s slides explicitly define deficiency as clauses minus existential variables and list complexity of MF(k) for fixed k≥2 as an open question. The editorial target isolates polynomial-time membership.
why: The target connects structural deficiency to the difficulty of recognizing minimal inconsistency under quantification.

import_provenance.original_title: Recognizing minimally false quantified formulas of fixed deficiency
import_provenance.original_statement: For each fixed k≥2, determine the complexity of recognizing closed prenex CNF quantified Boolean formulas that are false but become true after deletion of any clause, when the number of clauses minus the number of existential variables is k. Kleine Büning’s problem asks whether these restricted minimal-falsity tests have polynomial algorithms or remain computationally hard.
import_provenance.supplied_caveat: Remark: Deficiency1 is already polynomial-time decidable; the fixed-k problem is known to lie in DP.
